title: Fix billing edge cases for prefix prefetch and KV-cache batch aggregation
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: We are seeing billing and quota enforcement mismatches when requests hit prefix prefetch or KV cache and are then aggregated into GPU batches. In several customer incidents the dashboard shows significantly higher token usage than the runtime actually executed (or vice versa) and quota checks behave inconsistently for batched requests across tenants.

Root cause hypothesis: Metering currently samples token counts from the batch aggregator after batching occurs. The batching layer receives per-request request envelopes but in the current pipeline token accounting is performed on 'raw' sequence lengths or after naive aggregation rather than after cache-resolution/duplication removal. Two concrete failure modes observed: (1) Cached prefix/prefetch responses are being counted as billable input tokens multiple times when the same cached prefix is reused across requests inside the same batch. (2) KV cache hits reduce actual compute but the post-batch metering still sums the original requested sequence length and attributes the cost to each request rather than de-duplicating. Additionally, quota/rate-limiter checks are being applied at batch boundaries that let aggregated batches exceed individual tenant quotas before per-request attribution and enforcement.

Why this matters: Incorrect per-tenant billing and quota enforcement is high-severity for enterprise customers (overruns, unexpected charges, and SLA violations). It also complicates root-cause analysis for cost regressions and undermines confidence in the Console metering dashboards.

Repro steps (short):
1) Enable prefix prefetch or KV cache in a test runtime; deploy two test clients that request the same prefix in quick succession.
2) Force the requests to coalesce into a single batch by reducing batching timeout (test bench uses batch window 8ms).
3) Observe billing metrics: per-request input tokens reported in /billing/metrics and per-route dashboards.
4) Compare runtime actual GPU token compute (from trace) vs billed tokens.
Expected: billed tokens == sum of de-duplicated billable tokens per origin. Observed: billed tokens > actual compute (duplicate counting) or quota enforcement delayed until after batch-level accounting.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Move final billable-token calculation earlier in the request pipeline: perform per-request cache-resolution (prefix + KV cache lookup) at ingress, compute an explicit 'billable_input_tokens' and 'billable_output_tokens' for each request after cache hits are known, and attach these fields to the request envelope before batching.
- Change batch aggregator to sum billable_* fields rather than raw token lengths and ensure it emits per-request attribution records that mirror the envelope values.
- Update rate limiter to validate and decrement per-request quotas at ingress using the computed billable_* values (fail fast if quota would be exceeded), while still allowing batched execution for throughput. Ensure quota enforcement is deterministic and not delayed until after a batch executes.
- Add server-side instrumentation to assert invariants in canary: sum(billable_* per request) == billed_tokens_emitted_by_aggregator and billed_tokens_emitted_by_aggregator == runtime_compute_tokens +/- allowed-quantization-tolerance.
- Implement migration/adjustment tooling to reconcile any customers impacted by historical overcharges (see next section).

Trade-offs considered:
- Doing cache-resolution before batching slightly increases ingress CPU/lookup load (we'll move border cache checks to a fast path and reuse existing cache layers), but avoids expensive billing corrections and preserves predictable quotas.
- Alternative: instrument dedup at aggregation time. Rejected because aggregator currently lacks stable per-request cache hit semantics and it would be brittle across runtime variants.

Backwards compatibility: The change preserves the request envelope format (we add new internal-only fields). Backfill/migration of historical metrics may be required for accounts flagged as impacted.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests that compute billable_* values for combinations of cached prefixes, full cache misses, and mixed KV hits/misses
End-to-end testbench that runs against canary runtime with aggressive batching and validates billed tokens == compute tokens within tolerance
Console dashboards and per-route breakdowns show corrected token counts for canary and do not regress other metrics
Rate limiter rejects requests when per-request billable tokens would exceed quota (test cases for small/large requests)
Migration plan and customer communication draft approved by SRE and Billing team
implementation_notes: Add billable_input_tokens and billable_output_tokens to RequestEnvelope (internal flag) in runtime proto v2; default to existing behavior when flag is absent
Perform prefix/KV cache lookup at ingress path (fast path) and set envelope fields before building batch key
Modify aggregator to sum and emit per-request billable_* fields to metering pipeline; do not derive billing from post-aggregation token lengths
Update rate-limiter middleware to run quota checks against billable_input_tokens + billable_output_tokens at ingress and return quota_exceeded early
Add integration tests in runtime-testbench repo and a canary deployment to cluster billing-canary with tenant-level synthetic load
Create reconciliation job (billing-reconciler) to scan last 90 days for tenants flagged in initial investigation and compute delta adjustments for invoicing team
risk: Medium-high: touching billing and quota path could cause false-positive rejections or billing regressions if the billable calculation has edge cases (e.g., streaming partial cache hits, tool-calling that triggers immediate output). Mitigation: canary, strict invariants, feature flag rollout and safepoints for canary rollback.

2025-11-06 - Lin Zhao (SRE): Design LGTM with one note: ensure the ingress cache lookup has a hard cpu budget and early fail if lookup cost would violate latency SLOs. We'll add rate-limit guard for cache-prefetch path.

2025-11-08 - Diego Morales: Initial PR opened to add envelope fields and ingress lookup. Unit tests cover simple prefix reuse and pure misses. Need help wiring meter pipeline emitters for per-request attributes.
2025-11-10 - Eric Nguyen (Billing): Please add a flag to opt-in historical reconciliation for customers where overcharge delta > $50. We also need audit logs for any automated billing adjustments.

2025-11-12 - Diego Morales: Canary deployed to billing-canary cluster. Running synthetic suite (100k requests) now. Early results: billed tokens deviate from runtime compute by < 0.2% in canary vs 4-8% on master. Continuing monitoring.
